title: 9. The United States Is Going South w/ Lawrence Hamtil & Douglas Ott

reader_summary.headline: Hello and welcome once again to the Best Anchor Stocks podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hello and welcome once again to the Best Anchor Stocks podcast. Before going into today's episode, let's hear from our sponsor. Are you paying too much to trade options? If you're not trading on public.com, the answer is yes.

key_points.text: Public is the only platform where you earn a rebate on every option contract traded.
key_points.evidence_quote: Public is the only platform where you earn a rebate on every option contract traded, and that's in addition to no commissions or per contract fees.

key_points.text: There's no one else out there paying trading rebates, so you won't find a better deal.
key_points.evidence_quote: There's no one else out there paying trading rebates, so you won't find a better deal.

key_points.text: Bottom line, if you're paying more than $0 to place an options trade, then you're paying too much.
key_points.evidence_quote: Bottom line, if you're paying more than $0 to place an options trade, then you're paying too much.

key_points.text: Today I have with me Doug and Lawrence from the Preferred Shares podcast.
key_points.evidence_quote: Today I have with me Doug and Lawrence from the Preferred Shares podcast.

thesis: The speakers argue that a long-term trend of population and business moving from the North and Midwest to the South and Southeast is driven by factors such as warmer climates, favorable tax treatments, air conditioning making the environment habitable, and the interstate highway system leveling the infrastructure playing field. This shift, which has occurred over several generations since the post-World War II period, has resulted in southern states closing the economic gap with the national average and attracting major companies like Walmart and FedEx.
